records.transcript:
Good morning,

I write in relation to your request requesting:


“Please treat this as a request under the Freedom of Information Act

2000 for recorded information, excluding personal data and excluding any material for which the appropriate handling route is the separate subject-access request already open. The site is Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy’s Church, Cardiff (approx. ST 168 733), and the period is 1 November to 31 December 1988 inclusive.



Please search the relevant South Wales Constabulary / predecessor-force and successor holdings, including any transferred records available to the Force, for existing non-personal records that refer to the site or the events associated with its possession and demolition. Relevant record types, if held, include:

1. incident or occurrence logs and control-room records; 2. deployment, duty or operational logs and any record identifying whether officers attended; 3. correspondence between police, the local authority, landowner/developer, court enforcement officers or other public bodies about the site; 4. any recorded liaison or request for police assistance connected with possession, eviction, demolition, public order or the handling of complaints; and 5. records-transfer, retention or disposal entries for the relevant operational record series, if the responsive records are no longer held…”


It is not possible to progress your request at this time, as clarification is needed from you to enable us to locate the information you have asked for.

Please could you provide some information as to the individuals or entities involved in the occurrences at Ty Mawr from 01/11/1988 – 31/12/1988. We are currently liaising with our legacy crime team and they require this information to carry out a search on their records. Useful information would include any names, dates of birth, or addresses of any persons involved.

In line with the Freedom of Information Act 2000 Section 10(6), the 20 working day timescale will be suspended until the required clarification has been received, restarting on the date when the information is received.  If we do not receive clarification from you then your request will be closed 40 working days from the date of this email.

Kind regards,

Karen

Dear Requester,

With regard to the three remaining points noted below:

1) If you would like to order scans of these items, please complete and return the attached order form. While I cannot confirm a quote for this order before receiving a completed order form, an order of these three items would likely require four research-quality scans. As per the attached price list, we waive fees for orders requiring fewer than five research-quality scans for personal, non-commercial use.

2) As has been noted, our searches have not been limited to the registered files. No further information related to this is held beyond what is noted in the archive catalogue.

3) As noted in my emails of 29 September and 6 October, the item Archive Number 6364275 from the Emergency Recording Collection has been physically examined and does not relate to Great House Farm, Llandough. As noted (correctly) in the archive catalogue, it relates to Great House, Bonvilston.

All the best,

Adam Coward

Research enquiry — Bute Estate records GB 0210 BUTE / D153 / D219: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth — 1877 split and 1916 tenancy
Enquiries Service
The National Library of Wales

I am researching the title history of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Glamorgan, adjoining St Dochdwy’s churchyard (approx. ST 167 733).

Glamorgan Archives (Louise Hunt, ref. 2026/4097, 24 September 2026) has confirmed that the following references are yours, not theirs, and has directed me to you:

1. D153 — Deeds relating to premises in p. Llandough, co. Glam., comprising a dwelling house adjoining the churchyard, 1811 (D153/1–2), and land (D153 onwards, including items sometimes cited as D153/4–8).
2. D219 — Llandough manorial leases and agreements.
3. The main Bute Estate deposit, GB 0210 BUTE (deeds to 1937; Glamorgan / Cardiff rentals).

I do not ask you to adjudicate title. I ask only whether the following instruments exist in your holdings, and for catalogue references, dates, parties, acreages, and whether a plan is attached.

A. The 1877 division
Does the Bute deposit contain a conveyance, agreement, or other instrument of about 1876–1877 by which the Marquess of Bute (or trustees) conveyed or contracted to convey the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres adjoining the churchyard at Llandough to Daniel Thomas (or Thomas and another), while retaining about 9 acres of agricultural land to the east?

B. The 1916 agricultural tenancy
Does the deposit contain a yearly agricultural tenancy, or counterpart, of 1916 from the Marquess of Bute to John Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough?
If yes:
- does the parcels clause describe the whole farm, or only the land Bute still owned after 1877?
- is there a plan?
- what acreage is stated?

C. Rentals 1877–1936 for this farm
Do Glamorgan / Cardiff / Llandough rentals in GB 0210 BUTE distinguish, after c.1877, between:
- a house/buildings holding (Thomas / later Williams), and
- a residual Bute field holding later passed to Western Ground Rents in 1938?

D. Anything that would show the two holdings were treated as one unit again before 1938.

Purpose. HM Land Registry first-registered titles WA231076 (30 November 1982) and WA240304 (23 February 1983; later amalgamated). The 1982/83 files treat the land as one farm. The family case is that Parcel A (house and about 10 acres) had already left Bute in 1877 and was not the land let in 1916, so the 1982 merged title cannot be the same unit as the 1916 tenancy. Your deeds and rentals are the estate-side evidence that can confirm or deny that.

I live in Patagonia and cannot visit Aberystwyth in person in the short term. I would be grateful for:
- catalogue references and a short description of any matching items;
- whether copies can be supplied, and the cost;
- if the 1916 tenancy is not in GB 0210 BUTE, any note of where Bute tenancy counterparts after 1910 were deposited.

This is a new enquiry. It is not a repeat of FOI/2026/11. Glamorgan Archives hold the 1938–44 Western Ground Rents plan/rental book (D696) and have already answered on their own Bute material.

UPDATE: FIREWORKS
RESPONSE FROM POLICE AND COUNCIL


**
------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Requester

Fireworks continue to cause unacceptable noise disturbances in our community.

I raised the issue at Full Council on Monday, emphasising the importance of both the Council and the Police working together.

You can watch my comments here.  (https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1JExrTZK3w/)

https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1JExrTZK3w/

On Wednesday, our village experienced another incident.

It is clear neither the police nor the Vale of Glamorgan Council have taken sufficient action to date to address this problem.

Both authorities have failed to fulfill their duties to protect our community.

I've written to both authorities to raise serious concerns.

You can read my letter below.
FAO: South Wales Police
Vale of Glamorgan Council

8th October 2026


Dear both

Illegal firework usage in Llandough

I’m saddened to report that another firework related incident took place in Llandough last night.

This is impacting some of the most vulnerable members of our community, causing distress to the elderly, small children and animals.

It is apparent that those responsible for setting off fireworks are not residents and instead come into the community from outside.

A lack of action to date is sending a message to those responsible that their behaviour is acceptable and will be tolerated.

There have been several instances in which fireworks have been set off past 11.00pm at night, in direct contravention of the law. There may also be other laws and regulations that have been broken.

I would therefore be grateful if you would:

- Outline full details of all firework-related incidents in the Llandough ward reported to your respective authorities within the past 24 months;

- Confirm all actions that were taken following those incidents to address the problems reported;

- Outline all actions proposed by your authorities to prevent inappropriate firework usage in the Llandough ward in future;

- Confirm all measures available to your respective authorities to detain and apprehend the individuals responsible for inappropriate firework usage in the Community of Llandough as well as any restrictions that may be imposed to prohibit those individuals from entering the Community boundary; and

- Confirm details of any powers conferred on your respective authorities which enable you to introduce additional regulations or byelaws to impose stricter restrictions prohibiting firework usage within the Community of Llandough.

I have not copied this message to our PSCOs because they are not responsible for operational decisions, and as such it would be unfair to attribute blame to them for the failure to address this problem.

However, I reiterate my request for your respective authorities to meet with me at the earliest convenience to discuss this ongoing problem, with an invitation also extended to our PCSOs.

Thank you for your consideration of this matter, and I look forward to your prompt response.

Kind regards,

Cllr George Carroll
Elected member

Llandough ward
Vale of Glamorgan Council
I'm pleased to report both authorities responded promptly.

The Police have confirmed a Problem Oriented Police Plan is being developed in conjunction with our PCSOs.

The Inspector has confirmed he'll update me in due course, with further escalation promised if this proves insufficient.

The Council too have agreed to take part in a multi-agency meeting to address the problem.

The time for discussion has long passed.

We need to see surveillance and enforcement, so that those responsible for these disturbances know their behaviour will not be tolerated.

As a community, it's vital we keep up the pressure.


**
------------------------------------------------------------

NEXT WEEK: Penlan Road
temporary traffic lights

Temporary traffic lights will be in place on Penlan Road on Tuesday 13th October to allow for Welsh Water works to be carried out safely.

They will operate from 9.30am to 2.30pm.

The lights will be situated outside the Memorial Hall, with Spencer Drive and Cogan Pill Road also impacted.

The bus stops outside the Hall will be suspended due to proximity to the works.

Access will be maintained for residents at all times.

If anyone has further questions, please let me know.

Please see below for further information.
https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1Eqf5imB1i/

Llandough Hospital meadow

I've received many enquiries about the Llandough Hospital meadow, access to which has been restricted.

I've contacted the Health Board about this, as I know many residents enjoy using this route.

They've confirmed it has been fenced off as a temporary measure following misuse of the site.

They do not intend to close it permanently, but have restricted access while safety arrangements are reviewed.

A fortnight ago, I requested a likely timescale.

The person I spoke with said they were unable to provide one at present, but said they'd request an update.

I've chased them on this.

If anyone has further questions, please let me know.

The meadow has been a good benefit to our community and I’m pressing for it to be opened again as soon as possible.

Penarth Road water leak

Problems like the Penarth Road water leak require different agencies to work together.

The manhole from which the water is emanating is BT's responsibility, but the fault causing the leak is Welsh Water's responsibility.

The Council is in charge of highway safety, so they must make sure the algae forming in the discharge is cleared to prevent a slip hazard.

All responsible bodies must work together to fulfil their responsibilities, rather than blame each other.

I emphasised this to the Council this week.

Christmas Fayre
Saturday 14th November

Llandough’s annual Christmas Fayre is set to take place on Saturday 14th November.

With many local businesses operating stalls, it’s a great way to make a start to your Christmas shopping and support our local economy.

Huge thanks to Llandough Community Council for organising, it’s always a great event and this year promises to be no different.

Further details can be found above.

Community drop-in event:
20th October

Our next community drop-in event takes place at the Merrie Harrier on 20th October.

Like the last one, it'll start at 7.00pm.

The pub is a key asset to our community.

Tracey and the team do a lot for us - help return the favour by lending them your support.

You can see some of their midweek offers below!

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1EM9z5wbMs/

Our Plan for Llandough!


As your councillor, I'm working with you all to secure a better future for Llandough. Together, we have a plan to deliver for the village.

Our plan is making Llandough better by:

1. Sorting out the parking problems

To each recipient separately, in your own capacity as a current or potential holder, custodian or controller of relevant records:

This notice is addressed to each recipient individually. It is not a joint request, and it does not ask any recipient to speak for, investigate on behalf of, or answer in place of any other person or organisation. Each recipient is asked to respond only in respect of records within that recipient's own possession, custody or control, including records inherited from a predecessor organisation or retained on its behalf.

1. Nature and purpose of this notice

This is a formal preservation notice concerning documentary material relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy's, and the subsequent development of the site, including the area now associated with Church View Close.

It is not a claim form, is not service of proceedings, and is not intended to constitute or replace any FOI request, internal review, complaint, subject-access request or other statutory process already made to any recipient.

The purpose of this notice is to require the preservation of potentially relevant material while the documentary history, title chain, registration history, planning history, possession proceedings, demolition and subsequent development are being reconstructed.

A separate first-stage preservation notice has been issued or is being issued to Cadw / Welsh Government FOI, HM Land Registry Wales Office and DPO, Heneb / GGAT HER, RCAHMW, Vale of Glamorgan FOI Unit and DPO, Glamorgan Archives, South Wales Police FOI, The National Archives, the Wales Office FOI team, and the National Library of Wales. Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd has received a separate preservation letter.

You are receiving this notice separately because the published documentary record places you, or a predecessor whose records may remain in your custody or control, within the documentary, legal, professional, administrative or development chain concerning this land.

2. Land and documentary scope

Please preserve, and do not destroy, alter, overwrite, discard, transfer out of custody without a recorded handover, or otherwise dispose of, any record within your possession, custody or control relating to the land or matters identified below.

The scope includes, without limitation, originals, copies, working papers, drafts, annotations, plans, photographs, negatives, films, tapes, maps, registers, indexes, correspondence, emails and attachments, electronic files, archived mailboxes, databases, metadata, internal notes, meeting records, instructions, client or matter files, survey material and other associated records.

The material requested includes:

1. Historical ownership, occupation and conveyancing

The 1877 split; the 1916 and 1939 tenancies; the 1938 Bute to Western Ground Rents conveyance; the 1969 Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust conveyance; and any plans, schedules, abstracts, searches, correspondence or other documents relied upon in relation to those transactions.

2. Possession proceedings and subsequent litigation

The 1955 High Court and 1962 Cardiff County Court possession orders; the 1974 proceedings; BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2; House of Lords leave papers, including YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536; and Buckler v United Kingdom (1989), including associated correspondence, instructions, evidence, plans and working papers.

3. Land registration

The first registration of WA231076, including the application dated 30 November 1982; the first registration of WA240304, including the application dated 23 February 1983; subsequent amalgamation, transfer or closure; and every plan, conveyance, abstract, search, application, correspondence trail or professional file relied upon in connection with those registrations or changes.

4. 1988 possession and demolition

The taking of possession on or about 29 November 1988 and the demolition commenced on or about 6 December 1988, including any planning, listed-building, heritage, police, enforcement, media, contractor, survey, photographic or inter-agency liaison material.

5. Planning and subsequent development, 1989–1996

Planning application 89/01396/OUT; reserved matters application 92/00671/RES; conditions 16–18; GGAT / Cotswold Archaeology material; records concerning any section 52, section 106, planning obligation, local land charge or equivalent instrument; and the transfer from BP to Ideal Homes dated 3 December 1993, together with all associated plans, correspondence, approvals, agreements, searches and completion material.

6. Family records

Records concerning Mary Doreen Williams (died 1983) and William Buckler, insofar as those records relate to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, the land described above, its occupation, ownership, possession, disposal, registration, development or demolition.

3. Predecessor and inherited files

Where you hold, or may hold, a file originating with a predecessor, successor, merged practice, affiliated practice, client or other entity, that material is also within scope.

This includes, without limitation, records originating from:

Loosemores of Cardiff; Robbins Olivey & Blake Lapthorn / Blake Morgan; Linklaters & Paines; Debenham Tewson / DTZ / Cushman & Wakefield; Wyn Thomas + Partners; Ideal Homes Wales; BP Properties; BP Pension Trust; Cotswold Archaeological Trust; Cardiff Bay Development Corporation; and South Glamorgan County Council.

The reference to a predecessor file does not assert that you necessarily hold such a file. It identifies material for which a reasonable custody or succession inquiry should be made where applicable.

4. Preservation steps

Please take reasonable steps to prevent the routine destruction, deletion, alteration or overwriting of potentially relevant material, including material held in archived mailboxes, legacy systems, off-site storage, document-management systems, backup repositories and other electronic or physical stores.

Where relevant material has been transferred to another repository, archive, successor organisation or third party, please preserve the information necessary to identify the transfer and its current location, including any accession, file, box, reference or custody details.

We assert our claim to Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), in particular what the family calls Parcel A, and we ask every body that holds a record or made a decision about it to respect that claim by answering for its records, decisions and representations. I have also completed your online enquiry form, so the request is in your preferred channel.

records.transcript:
Dear Bona Vacantia FOI Officer,

This is a request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000.

I am researching the history of Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, near Penarth (historically Glamorgan; South Glamorgan from 1974 to 1996; now the Vale of Glamorgan), and of the land and woodland around it. My aim is to identify and preserve every surviving record of how this land changed hands, who made each decision, and on what record.

Background, from public sources:
- Western Ground Rents Ltd (company no. 00342092) is reported to have bought the Bute family's urban estate in 1938. It let farm land at Llandough from 1939, and it conveyed land at Llandough to the BP Pension Trust by a conveyance recited in HM Land Registry's records as dated 31 December 1969.
- On 26 June 1996 its members placed it in members' voluntary liquidation, together with other dormant companies whose registered office was BP House (London Gazette, issue 54455, 3 July 1996, pages 8979 and 8982). The final meeting was called for 16 May 1997 (London Gazette, issue 54739, page 4683), and the company was dissolved in 1997.

Please tell me whether the Bona Vacantia Division (or the Treasury Solicitor, before the Government Legal Department was formed) holds any information about this company, and in particular:

1. Whether any property, right or interest of Western Ground Rents Ltd was referred to your Division, or vested in the Crown as bona vacantia, on or after its dissolution. This includes freehold land, woodland, freehold reversions on leases, ground rents or rentcharges, and any reserved mines and minerals, and especially anything at Llandough, Leckwith, Cogan or Penarth.

2. For any such property: when and how it came to your notice (and who referred it, if a company or public body); what was done with it (sale, transfer, disclaimer under section 656 of the Companies Act 1985 or section 1013 of the Companies Act 2006, or retention); the date and the instrument; the buyer or transferee and the price, if a company or public body; and the record of the decision, with the role of the officer who approved it.

3. Any enquiry, application or correspondence about the company's property received since 1997 (for example from HM Land Registry, a local authority, a developer, a charity or a BP group company), with its date, the enquirer if a company or public body, and your reply.

4. Whether any application was made to restore the company to the register, and any letter your Division issued in connection with it.

5. If your Division held records about the company that are no longer held: when they were destroyed or transferred, under which retention schedule, and the record authorising that.

A "not held" answer to any part would be just as useful as a positive one. If anything is withheld, please name the exemption relied on for each part. Copies by email are ideal.

Please reply within 20 working days, by 17 November 2026.

Yours faithfully,

Requester

Search terms: "Great House Farm", "Tŷ Mawr", "Ty Mawr", "Llandough", "Penarth".

records.transcript:
Dear Welsh Local Government Association,

I am researching the history of Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, and how public bodies dealt with the farm and the land and woodland around it. My aim is to identify and preserve every surviving record.

I understand that the WLGA may not be a public authority under the Freedom of Information Act 2000, so this is a request for your voluntary help.

Please tell me whether the WLGA holds, or knows who holds:

1. Any guidance, circular or advice note issued to Welsh councils by the WLGA or its predecessors (including the Assembly of Welsh Counties and the Council of Welsh Districts), between 1974 and 2000, on acquiring, accepting or developing land whose title was disputed or unregistered, or where an occupier claimed title by possession; or on registering land as a town or village green where its ownership was disputed.

2. Any record of how the land of South Glamorgan County Council at Llandough, Leckwith and Cogan was allocated between Cardiff and the Vale of Glamorgan at the reorganisation of 1 April 1996 (Local Government (Wales) Act 1994; Local Government Reorganisation (Wales) (Property etc.) Order 1996), including any agreement, schedule, or dispute referred to the associations or to the Residuary Body for Wales. Press reports from 1994 and 1995 (South Wales Echo) describe South Glamorgan County Council acquiring about 125 acres of woodland and farmland between Leckwith and Llandough from the Land Authority for Wales. I am trying to establish which successor council received that land, and on what record.

3. Any record mentioning Great House Farm, Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, Western Ground Rents Ltd, BP Properties Ltd, or the case BP Properties Ltd v Buckler (Court of Appeal, 1987).

4. Where the archives of the Assembly of Welsh Counties are now held. (I understand that papers of the Council of Welsh Districts are at the National Library of Wales.)

5. If any of the above was held but has been destroyed or transferred: when, and under which retention policy.

A short "not held" would be just as helpful as a positive answer. A reply by 17 November 2026 would be much appreciated.

Thank you for your help.

Yours faithfully,

Requester

records.transcript:
Dear Lambeth Palace Library / Church of England Record Centre,

I am researching the history of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, the farm next to St Dochdwy's church, which was demolished in 1988. I am trying to establish, from the records, how the land around the church and the farm was held, exchanged and transferred, and by whom.

Two catalogue entries appear to relate to church land at Llandough:
(a) Lambeth Palace Library ECE/6/3/372/CD27551 (1 March 1890): "Leckwith St James R with Llandough R & Cogan R. re. T. R. Thompson";
(b) The National Archives MAF 11/55/5333: "Order of exchange of lands. Place: Llandough, Glamorgan. Parties: Major H H Lee and T R Thompson" (11 September 1879).

The Bute Estate held the freehold of Great House Farm until a conveyance on sale to Western Ground Rents Ltd dated 25 December 1938 (recited in a 1965 contract).

I would be grateful for your voluntary help with the following:
1. File ECE/6/3/372/CD27551: a short description of its contents (for example, whether it concerns glebe, an exchange of land, or a sale), its extent, whether it contains any plan, and a quotation for copies of any plan or conveyance in it.
2. Whether the Ecclesiastical Commissioners' records hold any file on the 1879 exchange between Major H. H. Lee and T. R. Thompson (MAF 11/55/5333), if it concerns Llandough-juxta-Penarth rather than Llandough near Cowbridge, or any other exchange, sale or purchase of glebe at Llandough-juxta-Penarth, with the file references.
3. Any glebe terrier, glebe plan or tithe-related file for Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Leckwith or Cogan held in the Ecclesiastical Commissioners' or Queen Anne's Bounty records, with references.
4. Any correspondence between the Ecclesiastical Commissioners and the Bute Estate (the Marquess of Bute or his agents) about land at Llandough or Leckwith, with references.
5. Any manorial records for Llandough or Leckwith held by the Library or the Record Centre.
6. Whether any record in the scope above is known to have been transferred to another repository (for example, the Representative Body of the Church in Wales after disestablishment in 1920, the National Library of Wales or Glamorgan Archives) or destroyed, with the date and the record of the transfer or destruction where held.

I understand that Lambeth Palace Library and the Church Commissioners are not subject to the Freedom of Information Act 2000, so this is a request for your voluntary help, and I am happy to pay normal copying charges. Catalogue references and a short description of each item would be ideal, even without copies. If you hold nothing, a short note saying so would be equally helpful. A reply by 17 November 2026 would be much appreciated.

Yours faithfully,

Requester
